learning_objectives.objective: Apply the commutative property to generate equivalent algebraic expressions.
Apply the associative property to generate equivalent algebraic expressions.
Apply the distributive property to generate equivalent algebraic expressions.
Identify when two algebraic expressions are equivalent by substituting various values for the variables and comparing results.
Write numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents to represent given situations.
Evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents using order of operations.
Substitute specific values for variables in algebraic expressions.
Evaluate algebraic expressions using the conventional order of operations when no parentheses specify a particular order.
Evaluate expressions that arise from real-world formulas by substituting given values.
Identify parts of algebraic expressions using mathematical terms including sum, term, product, factor, quotient, and coefficient.
Recognize one or more parts of an algebraic expression as a single entity for computational purposes.
Write algebraic expressions that record operations with numbers and variables to represent mathematical situations.
Write equations of the form x + p = q to represent real-world and mathematical problems involving nonnegative rational numbers.
Write equations of the form px = q to represent real-world and mathematical problems involving nonnegative rational numbers.
Solve equations of the form x + p = q where all values are nonnegative rational numbers.
Solve equations of the form px = q where all values are nonnegative rational numbers.

Apply substitution to determine whether a specific number from a given set makes an equation true.
Apply substitution to determine whether a specific number from a given set makes an inequality true.
Use variables to represent numbers when solving real-world problems.
Write expressions using variables when solving mathematical problems.
Explain that a variable can represent an unknown number in an expression.
Explain that a variable can represent any number from a specified set depending on the context.

Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions.
Represent solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.
Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another.
Write an equation expressing the dependent variable in terms of the independent variable.

Relate graph and table representations to their corresponding equations.

Calculate the area of special quadrilaterals by composing into rectangles or decomposing into component shapes.

Apply area calculation techniques to solve real-world problems involving composite shapes.

Define a ratio as a comparison between two quantities.
Use ratio language to describe relationships between two quantities in word form.
Express ratios using appropriate mathematical notation and terminology.
Define a unit rate as a ratio with a denominator of one.
Calculate unit rates from given ratios where the second quantity is not zero.
Use rate language to describe ratio relationships in real-world contexts.
Calculate a percent of a quantity using the rate per 100 interpretation.
Solve problems to find the whole when given a part and the percent.
Create tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements.
Calculate missing values in tables of equivalent ratios.
Plot pairs of values from ratio tables on the coordinate plane.
Compare ratios using tables.
Solve unit rate problems involving unit pricing.
Solve unit rate problems involving constant speed.
Convert measurement units using ratio reasoning.
Transform units appropriately when multiplying quantities.
Transform units appropriately when dividing quantities.
Identify statistical questions as those that anticipate variability in data and account for it in answers.
Recognize that measures of center summarize all values in a data set with a single number.
Recognize that measures of variation describe how values in a data set vary with a single number.
Recognize that data collected to answer a statistical question forms a distribution.
Identify the center as a characteristic that describes a data distribution.
Identify the spread as a characteristic that describes a data distribution.
Identify the overall shape as a characteristic that describes a data distribution.
Create dot plots to display numerical data on a number line.
Create histograms to display numerical data.
Create box plots to display numerical data on a number line.
Describe the nature of attributes under statistical investigation including measurement methods and units.
Calculate quantitative measures of center including median and mean for numerical data sets.
Calculate quantitative measures of variability including interquartile range and mean absolute deviation.
Describe overall patterns in data distributions with reference to the context.
Identify striking deviations from overall patterns in data with reference to the context.
Select appropriate measures of center based on the shape of the data distribution and context.
Select appropriate measures of variability based on the shape of the data distribution and context.
Report the number of observations in a data set as part of statistical summaries.
Explain the meaning of quotients when dividing fractions by fractions.
Compute quotients when dividing fractions by fractions using standard algorithms.
Solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
Use visual fraction models to represent division of fractions by fractions.
Write equations to represent word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.

Calculate distances between points with the same first coordinate using coordinates and absolute value.
Calculate distances between points with the same second coordinate using coordinates and absolute value.

Position integers and rational numbers on vertical number line diagrams.
Position pairs of integers and rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

Recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself.
Recognize that 0 is its own opposite.
Identify which quadrant contains a point based on the signs of its coordinates.

Distinguish between comparisons of absolute value and statements about numerical order.
Explain inequality statements in terms of relative positions on a number line.

Define absolute value as the distance from zero on a number line.

Explain the meaning of order statements for rational numbers by describing the relationship between the values in real-world contexts.

Use negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts.
Explain the meaning of zero in various real-world contexts involving positive and negative numbers.

Calculate the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12.
Apply the distributive property to express sums with common factors as multiples of sums with no common factors.

Subtract multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm.
Multiply multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm.
Divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm.
